advances: Counterexample to pointwise whole-assigned-fiber response payment even after maximizing over active menus.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
At the triangle source the first theorem gives the three unique continuous directions, their spanning positive balance, their proper own cuts, and their saturated outside patterns. The second theorem supplies the tied parameters $L_h$ and exact midpoint assignment of $D$ to source $0$. Choose one normalization for the normal of each direction, with its ambient tilt scaled the same way. This choice does not affect response probabilities: positive rescaling multiplies the normal and inversely scales its threshold derivative and the coefficient needed in a raw balance. All caps in a given direction have identical positive $S_j$, because their own plane and width agree and their outside coarea vanishes. Summing raw weights in each direction reduces every balance to the one-dimensional nullspace of a rank-two matrix with three columns. That nullspace has a strictly positive vector, so every menu has the same positive total weights up to a common factor, and every such menu uses all three directions. Response normalization then fixes the same three totals even when directions repeat with different tilts. A menu using one witness tilt per direction exists.

At zero width, with mark barycentrics $y=(1-2t,t,t)$, take the affine cap coordinate for branch $i$ to be $l_i(X)=1-\sum_{j\ne i}\lambda_j(X)/(2y_j)$, where $\lambda_j(X)$ are barycentric functions. This vanishes at the mark and equals one at vertex $i$. The cap at threshold zero has area $q_i=4V\prod_{j\ne i}y_j$. Its area after a small threshold move $s$ is $q_i(1-s)^2$, so its own coarea is $2q_i$. For response weights $\theta_i$, balance is equivalent to vanishing of $\sum_i\theta_i q_i\,dl_i$ on the barycentric tangent plane $\sum_j d\lambda_j=0$. Writing $k_i=\theta_i q_i$ and $K=\sum_i k_i$, the coefficient of $d\lambda_j$ is $-(K-k_j)/(2y_j)$. These three coefficients must agree. Summing their implied $K-k_j$ identities gives $k_j=K(1-2y_j)$. Thus $\theta_i$ is proportional to $(1-2y_i)/q_i$. Substituting $y$ gives the stated formulas. Since $t<1/3$, one has $0<\theta_A<1/3$.

The active directions and own coareas converge to their zero-width values uniformly for the compact $L$ interval. The proper sections lie away from vertex transitions near the minimizing angles, and the smoothed coareas are averages of their continuous ordinary derivatives. The rank and positive balance persist, so the normalized branch response probabilities converge uniformly as well. Thus $\omega_A<3/8$ at the tied $L_h$ for all sufficiently small $h$. Exactly the branch $A$ caps capture all of $D$, completing the best-menu assertion.
statement:
In the tied positive-width four-fiber family, a balanced active menu at the triangle source is any finite selection of its active caps with positive raw coefficients $\lambda_j$ balancing their continuous normals $\sum_j\lambda_j u_j=0$. Let $S_j>0$ be the derivative of the full smoothed cap mass with respect to outward threshold displacement and assign response probabilities proportional to $\lambda_j/S_j$. Such menus exist, and every such menu assigns the same total response probability $\omega_A$ to caps capturing the entire assigned endpoint fiber $D$ at base $-1$. For each fixed sufficiently small $\sigma>0$ and all sufficiently small positive $h$,
$$
\omega_A<3/8<\Gamma_2=4/9 .
$$
At zero width the three branch response probabilities are $\theta_A=(4t-1)/(6t-1)$ and $\theta_B=\theta_C=t/(6t-1)$, where $t=(1+\sqrt{1-3\sigma^2})/6$. In this example the actual deepest sources occupy both parities and all their active caps have zero outside transition coarea.
title: Every balanced menu at a deepest triangle source can underweight its assigned whole fiber
